summary: Controlled area assessment. Descriptive metadata and report contents require the displayed information eligibility.

sections.title: SURVEY BASIS
sections.body:
**Archive interval:** Five growing-season image comparisons with two soil and vegetation sampling visits

**Instrumentation:** Multispectral imagery, shallow resistivity transects, soil moisture and temperature profiles, nutrient and metals panels, targeted residue screening, and fungal culture

**Study boundary:** An irregular pale-surface basin within managed boreal cover; the access route and local identifiers are held separately.

sections.title: OBSERVED VARIANCE
sections.body:
**Regrowth response:** Pioneer vegetation repeatedly established along the perimeter but showed reduced survival after crossing the stable central boundary. During the second visit, paired transplant baskets placed across the boundary showed a 61-percent reduction in root extension on the central side within 30 hours.

**Reversibility:** Affected baskets resumed ordinary extension after removal. Central-grid soil supported normal germination when transferred to the perimeter control station.

**Soil response:** Moisture, pH, major nutrients, soluble salts, and measured temperature remained within the range of nearby disturbed ground. Electrical resistivity was consistently elevated at shallow depth.

**Targeted screen:** No residue on the current analytical list, fungal isolate, or measured metal burden explained the observed boundary.

sections.title: INTERPRETIVE LIMITS
sections.body:
**Ordinary explanations retained:** Compacted mineral fill, seasonal frost behavior, past aggregate storage, and an untested organic contaminant remain plausible contributors to the long-term surface condition.

**Unresolved point:** The short-interval transplant response followed the surveyed boundary rather than soil origin, moisture, temperature, or visible drainage. The current record does not identify a chemical or biological carrier.

sections.title: DISPOSITION
sections.body:
**Finding:** Location-dependent, reversible suppression of plant growth associated with—but not transferred by—the central substrate samples

**Action:** Continue remote seasonal comparison. Any repeat transplant work requires continuous environmental logging and a blinded off-site soil control.

**Review status:** Active for passive comparison; formal review resumes when new imagery, access, or analytical data becomes available.

**Personnel control:** Ordinary field PPE and dust control remain sufficient for perimeter work.

sections.title: COORDINATE & SAMPLE SCHEDULE
sections.summary: Location references, custody details, and retained sample identifiers remain with the controlling office.
